newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Innogenetics launches first Easdaq IPO.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Innogenetics launches first Easdaq IPO.

text.p: Belgian biotechnology firm Innogenetics NV on Tuesday launched the first initial public offering on Easdaq, Europe's newest small cap market.

Innogenetics, which sells diagnostic tests for diseases such as HIV and Alzheimers, is offering up to 6,658,050 shares, or 32 percent of its issued capital, at between $10 and $12 each, Marcel Stappers of lead managers KB-Securities NV said.
He told a news conference a "green shoe" of a further 98,708 shares could be allotted in the case of strong demand.
The final price, which could exceed $12, will be fixed on November 26. The issue runs from Wednesday until November 25.
KB Securities analyst Ruth Devenyns said at $12 the issue price represented a discount of around 17 percent on the company's post-IPO value of 8.8 billion Belgian francs ($285.9 million).
The company should make a net profit of around 58 million francs in 1996 after losing 114 million francs in 1995. Profit should rise to 1.3 billion francs by the year 2000.
"Innogenetics is a strong buy," she said.

Innogenetics chief executive officer Hugo Van Heuverswyn said the company would in the next three years market 28 new diagnostic tests and was conducting clinical trials on a number of therapeutic techniques, such as skin and tissue repair.

Innogenetics hopes its shares will become the first quoted on Easdaq on November 28, although officials from the growth stocks market -- modelled on the U.S. Nasdaq market -- said another IPO was possible before that date.

"We need a pan-European market," Van Heuverswyn said. "When I founded this company 10 years ago I experienced how difficult it is to get money for a new business. If people are making the effort to create a European market...we should help."
Van Heuverswyn said the company ruled out a listing on Nasdaq, but earlier this year nearly went public on London's Alternative Investment Market (AIM).
Biotech companies on Nasdaq mainly offer therapeutic treatments. Innogenetics, because it had to earn its research money, started by developing and selling diagnostic tools.
"Fundamentally we are a biotech company which will offer therapeutics, (but) the (Nasdaq) market would not have understood us," he said.
Easdaq was first suggested to it by Belgian bank Kredietbank, one of Easdaq's shareholders, he said.
Kredietbank, which owns KB Securities, took a 16.1 percent stake in Innogenetics earlier this year to provide the company with ready cash ahead of the listing, he said.
Kredietbank's stake is being offered for sale along with 3,994,830 new shares.
